theme: Race conditions, deadlocks and thread safety

terms.definition: A bug where the result changes because two threads use the same data at the same time.
terms.example: A race condition made the counter wrong.
terms.code:
var balance = 100
let readA = balance  // thread A reads 100
let readB = balance  // thread B reads 100
balance = readA + 50; balance = readB + 20
print(balance)

terms.definition: A property of code that many threads can use at once without breaking its data.
terms.example: Thread safety protects the shared counter.

terms.definition: A freeze where tasks wait for each other forever, so none of them can continue.
terms.example: A deadlock froze the whole app.

video.description:
Learn to explain why concurrent code gives wrong or frozen results: Race Condition, Thread Safety & Deadlock, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Race Condition - A bug where the result changes because two threads use the same data at the same time.
Thread Safety - A property of code that many threads can use at once without breaking its data.
Deadlock - A freeze where tasks wait for each other forever, so none of them can continue.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Race Condition, Thread Safety & Deadlock in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Race Condition, Thread Safety, Deadlock 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Race Condition - A bug where the result changes because two threads use the same data at the same time.
한국어: Race Condition: 두 스레드가 같은 데이터를 동시에 써서 결과가 달라지는 버그

Thread Safety - A property of code that many threads can use at once without breaking its data.
한국어: Thread Safety: 여러 스레드가 동시에 써도 데이터가 망가지지 않는 코드의 성질

Deadlock - A freeze where tasks wait for each other forever, so none of them can continue.
한국어: Deadlock: 작업들이 서로를 영원히 기다려 아무도 진행하지 못하는 멈춤 상태

dialogue.title: The wrong counter
dialogue.setting: A like counter with a wrong total

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my `likes` counter shows 41 sometimes, and 42 other times.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That sounds like a race condition. Two threads change `likes` at the same time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But each one only adds one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Each thread reads the old number first, so one update gets lost. That is a race condition.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Make the counter safe. Thread safety means many threads can use it without breaking the data.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I will use a lock, then.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Careful! If two tasks hold locks and wait for each other, you get a deadlock.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A freeze. Every task waits for another one, so nobody can continue.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay. I want thread safety without a deadlock.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then keep the lock short and simple.
A race condition made the counter wrong.
